events.preview_text: Get ahead on social without losing room for a timely local update.
events.body:
Line up a week of posts, and still post today's local news when it happens.

Planning ahead and staying open to the moment can feel like opposites — get far enough ahead and you can't react, stay reactive and you never get ahead. Buffer is social media software that lets you do both.

It holds your planned posts in a queue, in the order they'll go out. When something timely comes up, you add it and drag it into place, and the rest shift down instead of being rewritten.

On the Free plan you can line up **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time — paid plans are unlimited. Whether that's enough to run a weekly queue is worth a look before you start.

Check the official Free plan, then decide.

events.body:
You line up a few posts ahead so there's always something going out.

Then something worth posting happens in the shop today — and fitting it in means reshuffling the schedule you just set. Planning and reacting pull in opposite directions: stay ahead and you can't move, stay flexible and you never get ahead.

Buffer is social media software that keeps your planned posts in a queue, in the order they'll go out. When something timely comes up, you add it and drag it into place — the rest shift down instead of being rewritten.

On the Free plan you can line up **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time; paid plans are unlimited. It's worth checking whether that's enough to run a weekly queue before you sign up.

events.preview_text: Line up your Facebook and Instagram posts, and still slot in today's news.
events.body:
You run your own social, and some weeks you'd rather not do it live every day.

Buffer is social media software that holds your planned posts in a queue, in the order they'll go out — Facebook and Instagram among them.

When something happens in the shop, you add a post and drag it to the front, and the rest shift down instead of being rewritten.

That's how Foster Coffee Company works it: far enough ahead that they're not scrambling to find content, yet free to click and drag in a last-minute post when the day calls for one.

On the Free plan you line up **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time — so ten each for Facebook and Instagram — and paid plans are unlimited. The plans page confirms exactly what's included, so it's worth a look before you start a weekly queue.
